case: BIT and VARBIT keyed grid edits preserve wire values and reject malformed input
contract: The app parser keeps bit(5)[] and bit varying[] edits as exact array text; the keyed update uses the fixed pg_catalog.bit[] and pg_catalog.varbit[] casts.
Zero-based bounds, varying element lengths, an empty bit string, and SQL NULL elements match native array_send bytes and preserve the declared column types.
A malformed bit element returns PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 22P02 and leaves the edited row and sibling row unchanged.
The built-in type OID census includes BIT and VARBIT in the supported array allowlist; only arrays that remain unlisted are expected to refuse decoding.

app_server_contract.command: rtk proxy cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-app --lib bit_array_grid_edit -- --include-ignored --test-threads=1

array_oid_census.command: rtk proxy cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-postgres --test integration array_contract::value_contract_builtin_array_oid_census_matches_decode_allowlist -- --include-ignored --exact --test-threads=1

remaining_builtin_refusal_matrix.command: rtk proxy cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-postgres --test integration array_contract::value_contract_unlisted_builtin_arrays_refuse_with_native_oracles -- --include-ignored --exact --test-threads=1

postgres_array_contract_suite.command: rtk proxy cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-postgres --test integration array_contract:: -- --include-ignored --test-threads=1
